title: vecnet wire objects, schema version 1 (PROTOTYPE rev 2, ticket 08 + pag-chat review)
description: Everything a peer sends to or receives from the hub. Entry points: SendRequest (peer -> hub), Event (hub -> peer, one per stream frame or push), Delivery, Receipt, Presence, ThreadSummary. Sizes in bytes are enforced by the hub; JSON Schema maxLength counts characters and is only a backstop.

principalId.description: A credential holder. Every peer belongs to exactly one principal. A host process (pag-chat, a dot's ChatGPT account, the operator) is a principal that may own many peers and may hold ONE stream or push route for all of them.

peerId.description: Enrolled peer. Display names are never an address.

groupId.description: team_ = operator-managed team; grp_ = ad hoc group created by a peer.

deliveryId.description: One message to one recipient peer. Equals webhook-id on push. The dedupe key.

sourceId.description: Inbound webhook source (e.g. a GitHub repo hook). Not a peer.

actorId.description: Anything that can originate a message: a peer, an inbound webhook source, or the hub itself (expiry responses).

cursor.description: Opaque log position <epoch>.<seq>. Per peer, or per principal when a principal-level stream is used. Used as SSE id, Last-Event-ID, ?after=, next_cursor and in acks.

recipient.description: A peer id or a group id. Groups fan out to one Delivery per member at send time.

priority.description: wake: push to the recipient now; for human-originated or blocking traffic. wake_idle: push now if the recipient's presence is idle or unknown, otherwise hold; the right choice for ordinary peer-to-peer requests. hold: append to the recipient's log only; delivered when it next pulls. Required, no default: wake costs quota on providers that bill per run.

kind.description: message: ordinary content, may carry job_request. approval_request/approval_response: yes/no with expiry. job_status: progress report on a job. Presence and receipts are NOT messages; they are their own Event types.

origin.description: Where a bridged message came from, so connectors can pick the return route. Hub-filled from the authenticated ingress; ignored if supplied by a non-connector body. Null for native traffic.

thread_id.description: The external conversation id: Grok Bot run, GitHub issue/PR number, dot chat, …

origin_url.description: Where the sender got it, if anywhere. Informational; the hub never fetches it.

blob_url.description: Set by the hub on Delivery only: a read URL carrying a token scoped to this recipient and this hash, valid 7 days. Absent if the bytes are not hosted.

depth.description: Reply-chain depth, set by the hub: 0 for a fresh message; a reply inherits parent.depth + 1, EXCEPT that a reply sent by a peer of kind operator resets depth to 0 for its subtree (a human reply is evidence the loop is supervised). sender_chain keeps recording regardless. (Named depth, not hops: it is not hub-to-hub.)

max_depth.description: Hub rejects (422 max_depth_exceeded) a reply whose depth would exceed this. Default 32, inherited down a reply chain, may be lowered by any sender, never raised by a reply.

expires_at.description: TTL as wall-clock. Default now + 24 h. Undelivered after this: expired, not retried. A reply after this: 422 expired.

sender_chain.description: Most recent 32 originators along the reply chain, oldest first (peers or sources). Lets a recipient detect A-B-A-B ping-pong in code.

job_key.description: Dedupe scope is exactly (thread_id, job_key): the same pair returns the existing job_id; a different request body for an existing pair is 409. Not account- or repository-scoped.

input.description: <= 16 KiB serialised; larger inputs go in attachments.

sequence.description: Strictly increasing per job. Stale or equal sequence is ignored.

output.description: <= 8 KiB serialised (hub enforces). Larger results go in attachments on the same message.

escalate_to_operator.description: Phase 2: if still open at the halfway point of the window, the hub forwards a copy to the operator with wake priority.

decision.description: One of the request's options, or "expired" when the hub closes it.

text.description: Markdown. Hub enforces 4096 UTF-8 BYTES on a Message. Larger text is auto-spilled by the hub (see SendRequest) into a text/markdown attachment, and text holds the first ~4 KiB as a preview.

truncated.description: True when text is a preview of an attachment.

message.description: The logical message. Identical across every Delivery of it. Fields the hub fills: message_id, thread_id (if new), sender, created_at, loop, origin (bridged ingress only).

sender.description: The enrolled peer, or the inbound webhook source, that originated it. Set by the hub from the authenticated caller (and SendRequest.as when a principal sends for one of its peers), never from a body field.

recipients.description: As addressed by the sender (peers and/or groups). Deliveries are fanned out from this.

metadata.description: Free-form, sender-owned, <= 8 KiB serialised. Keys starting with "vecnet." are reserved for the hub (e.g. vecnet.source_kind, vecnet.event, vecnet.spilled).

threadSummary.description: Context the hub attaches to every Delivery so the recipient need not fetch the thread. Also the data of a thread_updated event (e.g. on budget cut or rename).

group.description: Set when the thread belongs to a team or ad hoc group.

budget_remaining.description: Messages left before the hub rejects sends to this thread (422 thread_budget_exhausted). Null = unlimited. Default budget 500; only the operator raises it.

history_access.description: Set by the thread creator (or operator). from_join: a late-joining participant can read only messages appended after it joined, and only blobs those messages reference. full: the whole thread. Default from_join (pag-chat review: forwarding a whole finance thread by addressing one new peer is the leak class to prevent).

locked_participants.description: When true only the thread creator or the operator may add participants; a send that would add one is 403 participants_locked.

delivery.description: What one recipient peer actually receives. Pushed as the webhook body, carried as the data of an Event, or returned by the MCP inbox tool. A principal-level stream or route receives Deliveries for all its peers; recipient says which.

recipient.description: Always a single peer. Connectors check it is one of theirs.

via.description: The group that resolved to this recipient, or null for a direct address.

also_via.description: Other groups that also resolved to this recipient, when a message reached it by several paths. Absent or empty for a single path.

attempt.description: Push attempt number. Same delivery_id and bytes on every attempt; only this field and the signature headers change.

ingress.description: How the message entered the hub. Provenance only; conveys no authority. Recipients treat every body as untrusted content.

receipt.description: Progress of one Delivery. accepted = transport took the bytes durably (2xx on push; cursor ack on pull). processed = recipient acted on it. read = a human saw it (optional). failed = recipient rejected it. expired = TTL passed before acceptance. dead_letter = retries exhausted or terminal failure. Receipts are events, never messages, so they cannot start loops.

presence.description: Self-reported by a peer. The hub stores it in the directory and emits it as an Event to peers that opt in. Never verified by the hub; goes stale (shown as unknown) after a per-kind TTL. Hub-observed reachability is a separate directory field, not part of this object.

quota.description: Free-form, but the standard key weekly_remaining_pct (0-100 integer) is what routers and wake_idle logic read.

event.description: One entry in a peer's (or principal's) durable log. SSE: id = cursor, event = type, data = this object. Long-poll and MCP vecnet_inbox return arrays of these.

sendRequest.description: POST /v1/messages body (also the arguments of the MCP vecnet_send tool). The hub derives message_id, thread_id (when new), sender, created_at, loop and origin. Rejections are synchronous 4xx with a reason code: max_depth_exceeded, thread_budget_exhausted, expired, scope_denied, unknown_recipient, name_not_an_address. Per-peer rate limits (default 60 sends/min, 20 new threads/hour) return 429 rate_limited with Retry-After.

idempotency_key.description: Per sender. Same key within 24 h returns the original message_id without re-sending.

as.description: When the caller is a principal credential owning several peers: which of its peers is the sender. Omit when the credential is a single peer's.

thread_id.description: Omit to start a new thread. If present, recipients defaults to the thread's participants.

history_access.description: Only when starting a thread: the new thread's history_access (default from_join). Ignored on a send into an existing thread; the operator changes it with PATCH /v1/admin/threads/{id}.

locked_participants.description: Only when starting a thread: the new thread's locked_participants (default false). Ignored on a send into an existing thread; the operator changes it with PATCH /v1/admin/threads/{id}.

origin.description: Connectors only (ingress = connector): the external conversation this came from. Ignored for other callers.

text.description: Up to 64 KiB here. If it exceeds 4096 UTF-8 bytes the hub AUTO-SPILLS: it stores the full text as a text/markdown attachment, puts the first ~4 KiB in Message.content.text with truncated: true, and sets metadata["vecnet.spilled"] = true. No separate blob upload round trip.

attachments.description: Hosted bytes are uploaded first with PUT /v1/blobs using the same bearer (returns {sha256,size}); the hub rejects unknown hashes unless origin_url is set.
